items.desc: From a two-way air route to an eight-MoU haul, here is what Kathmandu got from Delhi, what it left on the table and what went missing altogether.

items.title: Nepal crash out of Asia Cup Rising Stars after 96-run defeat to Pakistan A
items.desc: Nepal were bowled out for 72 while chasing 169, suffering their second heavy batting collapse in three matches.

items.title: Delayed ordinances signal a rift between Nepal president and prime minister
items.desc: Sheetal Niwas questions the urgency of bypassing Parliament to amend the Press Council Act and Nepal Airlines Corporation Act, as constitutional experts warn against indefinite delays.

items.title: Tribhuvan University’s eligibility list for 681 colleges draws criticism
items.desc: Student representatives and faculty members question whether colleges lacking adequate infrastructure, teachers and students meet the criteria for expansion.

items.title: Faith, folk dances and festivities at Rukum West’s Digre Mela
items.desc: The annual fair at the Digre Sai Kumari Temple drew an estimated 100,000 devotees this year, bringing together communities for worship, traditional performances and celebration.

items.title: India agreements open new opportunities for Nepal’s tourism
items.desc: Tourism entrepreneurs expect two-way flights through Bhairahawa and the Ayodhya-Janakpur rail service to help double Indian visitor arrivals.

items.title: Nepal to import 20,000 tonnes of DAP fertiliser within a week
items.desc: The shipment is expected to boost supplies for winter crops, with the state-owned Krishi Samagri Company Limited saying existing stocks and incoming supplies will meet seasonal demand.

items.title: Ani Choying Dolma’s appointment to Lumbini Trust challenged in court
items.desc: Petitioners allege that the appointment violated eligibility criteria and due process, citing unresolved questions over her citizenship and a pending money laundering investigation.

items.title: Nepal forecast to receive above-normal precipitation this winter
items.desc: ICIMOD warns of increased rainfall in the foothills and heavier snowfall at higher elevations, raising the risk of floods, landslides and avalanches in parts of the western Himalaya.

items.title: Where Karnali’s traditions come alive
items.desc: Hundreds of years-old fairs across the hill districts offer a meeting place for worship, folk performances and community celebrations.

items.title: Why buying a first home is becoming a distant dream for young Nepalis
items.desc: House prices far outstrip incomes, while low bank valuations and hefty down payments put a first home beyond the reach of many salaried buyers.

items.title: Nepal to get an IIT campus under new education agreement
items.desc: Announced during Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India, the proposed campus is expected to strengthen cooperation in technical education, research and innovation.

items.title: Beyond Lumbini’s monasteries, a journey through village life
items.desc: New cycling routes take visitors through rural settlements, farmland, ponds and historic sites around Buddha’s birthplace.

items.title: Over 600 Nepali workers in Romania report pay and accommodation dispute
items.desc: Workers allege that a Romanian logistics firm is offering lower wages than those promised in their contracts and seeking to charge them for accommodation that was supposed to be free.

items.title: Taiwan’s elections not about China, but Beijing has a lot to say
items.desc: The ruling party’s Taipei mayoral candidate, labelled a separatist by Beijing and wanted by Chinese police, has become a target of Chinese denunciations ahead of Saturday’s polls.

items.title: Ayodhya-Janakpur train arrives with 1,000 passengers
items.desc: The Saryu-Kamala Express was flagged off by the prime ministers of Nepal and India in New Delhi on Monday before departing from Ayodhya.

items.title: Temporary cable crossings ease access to flood-hit villages in Gorkha
items.desc: Two suspension bridges were washed away by floods in the Budhigandaki river, leaving around 550 households struggling to access roads and transport essential supplies.

items.title: New Indian ports offer Nepal more options, but cost benefits remain unclear
items.desc: Businesses in Birgunj say inland freight charges, rail links and transit arrangements will determine whether access to Paradip and Kandla lowers trade costs.

items.title: Tenth National Games get underway with competitions in five sports
items.desc: Women’s cricket, men’s football, women’s basketball, tennis and swimming events begin ahead of the official opening on December 2.

items.title: Government plans more ordinances before convening Parliament
items.desc: The move is aimed at removing legal hurdles to projects to be showcased at an infrastructure conference in Kathmandu on December 9-10.

items.title: Karnali to host National Games, but not all sports will be played there
items.desc: About 6,500 athletes will compete in 384 events, though the province lacks facilities for several sports.

items.title: Q&A: The man behind Fapla on why the government should not run stadiums
items.desc: Subash Shahi, the man behind Dhangadhi’s cricket push, says the groundwork for the stadiums is done and the next three years will decide whether they get built.

items.title: 5.6-magnitude earthquake strikes near Nepal-Tibet border
items.desc: The earthquake was centred near Olangchung Gola in Taplejung district and struck at 7:17am on Tuesday. The EMSC put its magnitude at 5.3 and depth at 10km.

items.title: Explained: What are the various US federal and state probes faced by Nvidia and Jensen Huang?
items.desc: Nvidia and its CEO face investigations into alleged espionage links, antitrust concerns, accounting practices and possible export-control violations, as well as scrutiny from Congress and California authorities.

items.title: How a simple app makes QR payments easier to track
items.desc: To solve an inconvenience at his parents’ shop, 25-year-old Rohit Kumar Gupta developed an app that announces incoming digital payments aloud.

items.title: It takes some Rukum East villagers five days to visit their ward office
items.desc: Residents of four remote settlements in the district want a separate ward or merger with a neighbouring ward to end their hardship.

items.title: Why do women in literature keep turning into trees?
items.desc: From Greek mythology to contemporary fiction, women escape violence by becoming trees. These transformations reveal a deeper crisis of faith in humanity and the world it has built.

items.title: Inside one of Nepali cinema’s most enduring partnerships
items.desc: Actress Rekha Thapa and director Shabir Shrestha have forged a rare creative partnership across eight feature films over 25 years. Ahead of their new film, the two look back on what has kept it going.

items.title: Hearing on Dan Bahadur Karki’s reinstatement petition postponed after IGP fails to receive court notice
items.desc: The Supreme Court has rescheduled the hearing for Wednesday after Manoj Kumar KC did not receive a summons. Court tells attorney general to ensure summons is served and submit Cabinet documents.
